digest.definition: The subject joins communicative proficiency in one or more languages with study of their linguistics, cultures and societies from many disciplinary angles; the languages range from global to regional, indigenous and minoritised, past and present
distinctiveFeatures: The subject joins communicative proficiency in one or more languages with study of their linguistics, cultures and societies from many disciplinary angles; the languages range from global to regional, indigenous and minoritised, past and present
Immersive learning, physical or digital, in the target language and culture is a defining feature, often a year abroad, valued for language, cultural understanding and intercultural competence
It is intercultural and transnational by nature: ideas and events crossing borders, relations between countries, the effect of communities abroad on identities at home
Most students learn a language they do not yet command fully, and the language of study may also be a teaching medium, a gateway to the study of culture and society
It draws critical methods from the humanities and social sciences and combines readily with other SHAPE subjects and with STEM
It sets itself against Anglophone hegemony and native-speakerism, measuring proficiency by a framework such as the CEFR
Language learning is intensive, needs regular contact with proficient users and authentic material and asks for learner autonomy
Graduates go on to many sectors, from diplomacy and policy to translation, education, media and business

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: an outward-looking subject that values multilingualism, minority, sign and heritage languages, linguistic diversity beyond one standard form and rejects native-speakerism; it asks students to examine colonial and other injustices and prepares them for intolerance abroad (D1, 1.12 to 1.18)

uneven access to languages before university, so courses take beginners and heritage speakers; barriers to placements abroad (money, visas, caring, disability) met by reasonable accommodation or other immersion; alternatives to live oral assessment (D1, 1.13, 1.19 to 1.21, 3.20)

headed Sustainability: international perspectives on equality, peace and justice, four named UN goals (4, 5, 10, 16), climate and nature compared across cultures and the carbon cost of travel for placements (D1, 1.11, 1.22 to 1.25)

curiosity, adaptability and resilience from engaging other cultures; placements as enterprise learning; graduates as sensitive communicators, collaborators and users of language technology; employability through varied assessment (D1, 1.26 to 1.32, 3.21)

subjectSpecific.text: You are likely to finish this degree highly capable in your languages: confident speaking, writing, listening, reading and mediating between them.
You are likely to become alert to how the setting shapes what people say, to notice shifts in usage and what they signal and to cope when meaning is unclear.
You are likely to learn about the tools that support language work, such as translation software and online corpora, and you may become skilled with some of them.
You are likely to be able to appreciate and critically interpret many kinds of culture, from literature and film to everyday habits, local traditions and digital media.
You are likely to be able to explain, compare and mediate ideas and events that cross borders of country, culture or language, such as how two nations relate.
You are likely to learn to approach questions by comparing languages, cultures and societies, including regional and minority ones, not only national ones.

transferable.text: You are likely to grow more open-minded, able to see things as other people see them and to value views unlike your own.
You are likely to leave with the language and intercultural skills to live and work in other countries, especially if you spend time abroad during your studies.
You will build the habit of working on your own while still using guidance, thinking about your progress and acting on feedback.
You will learn to be a useful, effective member of a team.
You will grow in taking the initiative and organising yourself, including managing your time well.
You will learn good ways to find, organise and use evidence, data and information of many kinds.
You will become more analytical and questioning, able to work through problems, even ones with no single right answer.
You will get better at grasping ideas and building a case of your own.
You will learn to communicate clearly and in an organised way, in words and in other ways.
You will grow in intellectual honesty and independence, and get better at seeing where other people's arguments hold up or fall down.
You will develop your imagination and creativity.
You will understand academic honesty and the ethical duties you take on when you do research.
You will become confident and capable with digital tools and information.
You will take part in current debates about sustainability and the world seen from many places.

statements.about: high proficiency in the studied languages
statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically reach a high level in the language or languages studied, strong in producing, receiving, interacting and mediating, so they communicate in them with confidence and subtlety.

forPractitioner.text: The usual graduate profile includes a high command of each studied language across all four modes (production, reception, interaction, mediation), enough to communicate with assurance and finesse.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to finish this degree highly capable in your languages: confident speaking, writing, listening, reading and mediating between them.

statements.about: context, variation and ambiguity in communication
statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically understand the wider setting of communication, notice how usage varies and why it matters and can handle uncertainty and ambiguity when communicating.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates usually read communication in its context, are alert to variation in usage and its meaning and cope with uncertain or ambiguous exchanges.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to become alert to how the setting shapes what people say, to notice shifts in usage and what they signal and to cope when meaning is unclear.

statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically know about relevant language technologies, such as translation tools, language software and corpora, and some become skilled with them.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates usually know the relevant language technologies (computer-assisted translation, processing and learning software, online corpora) and some gain competence in them.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to learn about the tools that support language work, such as translation software and online corpora, and you may become skilled with some of them.

Purposes and characteristics of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically have an open outlook and can view the world as others do, so they understand and value more than one perspective.

forPractitioner.text: The usual graduate is open-minded and able to take other people's viewpoints, valuing a plurality of perspectives.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to grow more open-minded, able to see things as other people see them and to value views unlike your own.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically appreciate, analyse and critically interpret a wide range of cultural forms, products and practices, from local and national cultures to high, popular, material and digital culture and everyday customs.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates usually analyse and interpret critically a broad span of culture: community to national, high to popular, material and digital and the habits of daily life.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to be able to appreciate and critically interpret many kinds of culture, from literature and film to everyday habits, local traditions and digital media.

statements.paraphrase: Graduates typically grasp, mediate and compare ideas and happenings that cross national, cultural or linguistic borders, such as relations between countries past and present and analyse them.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates usually work with ideas and events that cross borders of nation, culture or language, understanding, mediating, analysing and comparing them, for instance relations between states.

forBeneficiary.text: You are likely to be able to explain, compare and mediate ideas and events that cross borders of country, culture or language, such as how two nations relate.

statements.paraphrase: Graduates develop imaginative insight and creativity.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates develop imaginative insight and creative ability.

forBeneficiary.text: You will develop your imagination and creativity.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates develop awareness of academic integrity and of the ethical duties of anyone doing research.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates develop awareness of academic integrity and the ethical obligations of researchers.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand academic honesty and the ethical duties you take on when you do research.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates develop digital literacy.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates develop digital literacy skills.

forBeneficiary.text: You will become confident and capable with digital tools and information.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates develop an appreciation of, and take part in, current debates on global sustainability and global perspectives.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates develop engagement with present-day debates on global sustainability and on global viewpoints.

forBeneficiary.text: You will take part in current debates about sustainability and the world seen from many places.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.about: enterprise attributes from engaging other cultures
statements.paraphrase: Because every student must engage with languages and cultures not their own, graduates will be curious and open, able to recognise and manage their own bias and will show enterprise attributes such as agility, flexibility, critical thinking, emotional literacy and digital skill; they will be able to adapt and keep learning, and facing uncertainty and failure builds resilience and initiative.

forPractitioner.text: Engaging with other languages and cultures is the means; the expected result is graduates who will be curious, aware of their own bias, agile and critical, emotionally and digitally literate, able to adapt and keep learning and resilient after facing risk and failure.

forBeneficiary.text: Working with languages and cultures unlike your own will make you more curious and open, help you notice your own bias and build flexibility, critical thinking, emotional awareness and digital skill; you will be able to adapt, keep learning and bounce back from setbacks.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.about: sensitive communication and mediation at work
statements.paraphrase: Students have a refined understanding of language and communication in real and virtual settings, notice the cultural and contextual factors shaping usage and through intercultural awareness and mediation will be able to work as sensitive communicators, negotiators and influencers in varied professional settings.

forPractitioner.text: Students build a refined grasp of real-world communication, including online, and of how culture and context shape usage; the expected result is that they will be able to act as sensitive communicators, negotiators and influencers at work.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how language works in real and online settings and how culture and context shape it, and you will be able to communicate, negotiate and influence with sensitivity in many kinds of job.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.about: cultural and digital literacy, collaboration, machine translation
statements.paraphrase: Graduates are culturally and digitally literate and will be able to find their way through and analyse language, culture and society in a connected, technology-heavy world; they gain collaborative skills across backgrounds, can lead by bringing sensitivity to language into work and work well with technology such as by revising machine translation output.

forPractitioner.text: The expected result is graduates who will be able to analyse language and culture in a digitally connected world, collaborate across linguistic, cultural and disciplinary lines, lead through attention to language and work productively with technology, for instance post-editing machine translation.

forBeneficiary.text: You will become culturally and digitally literate, able to make sense of language and culture in a connected world, work well with people from many backgrounds and use technology wisely, for example by checking and improving machine translations.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.appliesTo: undergraduates on joint or combined degrees
statements.paraphrase: Undergraduates taking the subject within a joint or combined degree will reach the core of the specific and general skills set out, will gain others from their other subject or subjects and may explore where the subjects overlap.

forPractitioner.text: For joint and combined honours, students will achieve the core of the subject-specific and generic skills and will add others from the partner subject; the overlap offers room for interdisciplinary work.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study languages alongside another subject, you will gain the core language and general skills, add others from your second subject and may explore where the two meet.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Languages, Cultures and Societies degree

statements.paraphrase: Providers will involve external reviewers in periodic review to get an outside view on changes and to make sure threshold standards are met and content suits the subject; externality is essential to UK quality assurance.

forPractitioner.text: In periodic review you will use external reviewers, both for an outside view on proposed changes and to confirm threshold standards are achieved and content fits the subject.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the provider in course review; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: content as a framework; designers stay open to change
statements.paraphrase: The content section is a framework for designers, not a list that has to be covered; because languages, evidence, technology and motives for learning keep changing, designers are told it is essential to stay open to new content and design.

forPractitioner.text: Treat the content section as a framework rather than a syllabus, and keep your course content and design open to change as languages, the evidence base, technology and learners' reasons for study move on.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: addressed to curriculum designers, not a standard the student reaches

headingPath: Characteristics of the study of Languages, Cultures and Societies

statements.paraphrase: Courses require students to take some autonomy and responsibility for building their proficiency by studying on their own; guided self-study and research let ideas grow beyond the classroom in a structured setting.

forPractitioner.text: Your course requires students to take a share of responsibility for their own language development through independent study, supported by guided independent study and research within a structured environment.

forBeneficiary.text: You must take some responsibility for your own language progress through independent study; guided study and research help you develop ideas beyond the classroom.

statements.about: Annex D for achievement above threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will perform well above the threshold; providers set their own evidence for this, and readers should refer to Annex D, which sets out the four honours classes for degrees at FHEQ level 6 and its Scottish equivalent, FQHEIS level 10.

forPractitioner.text: Expect most students to exceed the threshold; judge the higher classes by your own institutional method and refer to Annex D, which describes first, upper second, lower second and third class outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an instruction to readers judging classification, chiefly staff

statements.appliesTo: readers of the standards and course teams
statements.paraphrase: The standards set no curriculum; courses may weight the skills and knowledge differently or leave some out, so the standards must be read together with each course's documentation of its outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: The standards are not a curriculum: your course may weight the areas differently or omit some, so the standards must be read alongside your course documentation, which has to state its outcomes clearly.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: an instruction to readers of the standards, chiefly course teams

headingPath: Standard of achievement at threshold level: Language proficiency

statements.about: reading and listening to demanding long texts
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to follow a broad range of long, demanding texts and pick up what they imply as well as say, working towards or at CEFR C1.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to comprehend a wide variety of challenging, extended texts and grasp implicit meaning, working towards or at CEFR C1.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to understand long, challenging texts of many kinds and pick up meanings that are implied rather than stated.

headingPath: Standard of achievement at threshold level: Language proficiency

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to speak and write fluently and spontaneously without obvious searching for words, towards or at CEFR C1.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to express themselves fluently and spontaneously, rarely needing to search for words.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to express yourself fluently and on the spot, without often having to hunt for the right words.

headingPath: Standard of achievement at threshold level: Language proficiency

statements.about: flexible use across social, academic and work purposes
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to use the language flexibly and well for social, academic and professional ends.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to deploy the language flexibly and effectively across social, academic and professional settings.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to use your language flexibly and well in social life, in study and at work.

headingPath: Standard of achievement at threshold level: Language proficiency

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to write clear, well-organised, detailed text on complex topics, with controlled use of structure, linking words and cohesion.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to produce clear, detailed, well-organised text on complex topics, controlling organisation, connectors and cohesion.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to write clear, well-organised, detailed pieces on complex topics, linking your ideas smoothly.

headingPath: Standard of achievement at threshold level: Language proficiency

statements.about: translating complex texts from the target language
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to translate complex texts on many general and specialist subjects out of the target language, conveying nuance and implication.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to translate complex general and specialist texts from the target language, rendering nuance and implication.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to translate complex texts on general and specialist topics out of the language you study, keeping their nuances and implications.

statements.about: structures, registers and varieties of the language
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show some knowledge and an aware understanding of how each studied language is structured and of its registers and varieties.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show awareness and some knowledge of the structure, the registers and the varieties of each studied language.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will know about the structure of your language, its registers from formal to informal and its different varieties.

statements.about: sociolinguistic contexts of registers and varieties
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show awareness, understanding and some knowledge of the social settings in which different registers and varieties are met and used.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show awareness and some knowledge of the sociolinguistic settings where registers and varieties occur.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will understand the social settings where different registers and varieties of your language are heard and used.

statements.about: linguistic principles for analysing the language
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show awareness, understanding and some knowledge of the linguistic principles needed to analyse the language or languages studied.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show awareness and some knowledge of the linguistic principles used to analyse each studied language.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will know the basic principles of linguistics you need to analyse how your language works.

statements.about: knowledge of one or more cultures and societies
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show knowledge and understanding of at least one culture and society, usually deepened by residence abroad or another immersive experience.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show knowledge and understanding of one or more cultures and societies, typically deepened by residence or an alternative immersive experience.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will know and understand at least one culture and society linked to your language, usually deepened by time spent there or another immersive experience.

statements.about: sociocultural and sociolinguistic norms in other cultures
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show awareness, understanding and knowledge of differing sociocultural and sociolinguistic perspectives and norms in other cultures and societies.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show knowledge and understanding of the varied sociocultural and sociolinguistic norms and viewpoints within other societies.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will understand that other societies have their own social and language norms and that views differ within them too.

statements.about: comparing other cultures with one's own
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will show awareness, understanding and knowledge of how those cultures and societies resemble and differ from their own.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will show understanding of the likenesses and differences between the cultures studied and their own.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to say how the cultures you study are like and unlike your own.

statements.about: respect for cultural diversity and difference
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to handle cultural diversity and difference with sensitivity and respect, open to varied perspectives and worldviews.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to engage sensitively and respectfully with cultural diversity and difference, showing openness to other worldviews.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to treat cultural differences with sensitivity and respect, staying open to other ways of seeing the world.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to describe and assess the views and practices of their own and other groups, aware of the hidden values behind judgements and prejudice.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to describe and judge the views and customs of their own social group and of others, aware of the implicit values beneath judgement and prejudice.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to describe and assess how your own group and others think and behave, and notice the hidden values behind judgements and prejudice.

statements.about: adapting to sociolinguistic and pragmatic conventions
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to spot where sociolinguistic and pragmatic conventions differ, think about those differences and adapt their own communication.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to identify and reflect on differing sociolinguistic and pragmatic conventions and adapt how they communicate.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to notice when the social rules of talking differ, think about them and change how you communicate to fit.

statements.about: discussing culture drawing on encounters and media
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to explain, interpret and discuss aspects of culture and its practices, drawing on intercultural encounters, reading, film, social media and the like.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to explain, interpret and discuss culture and cultural practice with reference to encounters, texts, film and social media.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to explain and discuss aspects of a culture using what you have met in person, read, watched or seen online.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to cope with ambiguity in communication across cultures.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to manage ambiguity in cross-cultural communication.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to cope when communication between cultures is unclear.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to mediate effectively between cultures, keeping interaction positive by explaining differing views and handling ambiguity.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to mediate effectively between cultures, sustaining positive exchange by interpreting perspectives and managing ambiguity.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to act as a go-between for people from different cultures, keeping things positive by explaining each side's view and handling uncertainty.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to show that they know and understand at least one area of the target societies, such as their literature, culture, linguistic setting, history, politics, geography or social and economic make-up.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of at least one aspect of the target societies: literature, culture, language setting, history, politics, geography or social and economic structure.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to show what you know about at least one area of the places where your language is spoken: literature, culture, history, politics, geography, society or economy.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to use a range of critical methods to analyse and interpret varied cultural materials, media and forms of communication.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to deploy several critical methods when analysing and interpreting a variety of cultural materials and media.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to use different critical approaches to analyse and interpret many kinds of cultural material and media.

statements.about: how language and image work in context
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to explain how words, images and other modes of communication are put to use in particular social and cultural settings and for particular ends.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to account for the ways language, images and other modes are exploited in given social and cultural contexts and for given purposes.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to explain how words, images and other forms of communication are used to particular effect in particular settings.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to mediate between languages, showing cultural and plurilingual competence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to mediate between languages with cultural and plurilingual competence.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to mediate between languages, showing you understand the cultures and can move between several languages.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to take part in current debates, bringing historical, comparative and global perspectives to them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to contribute to present-day debates using historical, comparative and global perspectives.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to join current debates, bringing in history, comparison and a global view.

statements.about: evidence from sources in several languages
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to collect, handle and assess evidence and information from varied sources in different languages.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to gather, process and evaluate evidence from a range of sources across languages.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to find, work through and judge evidence and information from many sources, in more than one language.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to use digital resources and information technology appropriately to find information, communicate and support learning.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to make appropriate use of digital resources and IT for information, communication and learning.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to use digital resources and technology well to find information, communicate and help you learn.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to recognise and analyse problems and move towards resolving them.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to identify and analyse problems and work towards solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to spot and analyse problems and work towards solving them.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to convey information, ideas and arguments in speech and writing and by non-verbal means.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to communicate information, ideas and arguments verbally and non-verbally.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to put across information, ideas and arguments in words and in other ways.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to carry out independent research, organise relevant material and develop ideas into a fitting written argument or response.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to conduct independent research, organise relevant material and conceptualise ideas into an appropriate written argument.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to research a topic on your own, organise what you find and shape your ideas into a sound written argument.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to present formal written work with careful attention to effective language, referencing and layout.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to present formal writing that shows attention to effective language, referencing and layout.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to present formal written work that is well written, properly referenced and well laid out.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to show that they learn independently and manage their time well.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to demonstrate independent learning and effective time management.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to show that you can learn on your own and manage your time well.

statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to work in a team, framing joint tasks by agreeing aims, processes and steps, building ideas and solutions together and answering the strong and weak points of other arguments constructively.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to work as team members, framing shared tasks (aims, processes, steps), jointly building ideas and solutions and giving constructive responses to others' arguments.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will be able to work in a team: agreeing what you are aiming for and how, building ideas together and responding fairly to the strong and weak points in others' arguments.

statements.about: academic integrity and ethics in their own work
statements.paraphrase: At threshold, will be able to understand what academic integrity and ethics require and apply them to their own work, especially in reusing other people's research and writing.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates will be able to understand and apply academic integrity and ethics in their own work, notably when reusing others' research and writing.

forBeneficiary.text: By the end of your degree, as a minimum, you will understand academic honesty and research ethics and apply them in your own work, especially whenever you use other people's research or writing.
